# The Four Branches — questions for the owner

- 2026-10-12 · punctuation · The pilot's punctuation and word division match the second witness (the Williams-shaped cy.wikisource text) exactly, although the conventions say they are ours. Decided meanwhile: continue the pilot's practice, so the parts match.
- 2026-10-12 · mabinogi-002 · Col. 16: Evans prints a blank in "Arglwyd heb [ ] allu"; the Red Book reads "heb ef nyt oes allu". Decided meanwhile: supply "nyt oes" only (what the sense needs), with a note. Col. 14 "na thygyei idaw idaw": printed as written, with a note.
- 2026-10-12 · audio · No Middle Welsh voice chosen (a pilot clip job exists, unheard). Decided meanwhile: parts publish without audio.

## 2026-11-11 · mabinogi-002 · the 6-shaped w standing for /v/
Col. 14 l. 26 Evans prints "ny wydwn i 6arch" (the witness: "varch"). The establish rule (6-shaped w → w) gives "warch"; the
published pilot printed v in like places ("Vrth ual", "Y vely", "a'y vreic"). Decided meanwhile: follow the rule ("warch"),
the drafter's note to say it is *march* soft-mutated, spelt with the w-letter. The owner may prefer v where the sound is /v/.

## 2026-11-11 · mabinogi-003 · small open points
- "a'y dodi yn y carchar e hun" (col. 24): whose prison is not said, and *carchar* is unmutated after 'his' (Red Book *y garchar*). Decided meanwhile: `l`/`i` "his own", note says the referent is uncertain.
- "nit eidawaf y rodi y neb" (col. 22): rare; Red Book "nyt adawaf". Decided meanwhile: text as the White Book, read 'it is not mine to give', flagged uncertain.
- Published glossary entries *gelwit*, *gyweirwyt* say "3 sg. impersonal"; the 003 review uses "impersonal". Left unchanged (outside this part); the owner may want them aligned.

## 2026-11-11 · mabinogi-004 · small open points
- Col. 34 l. 21: "nat oed iawn udunt wy attal y mab ganthaw" — Evans prints singular *ganthaw* where the witness has *ganthunt*. Decided meanwhile: text as the White Book; the note will say so.
- Col. 37 l. 18: "Teirnon Toryfliant" against "Twryf Uliant" elsewhere in the part. Decided meanwhile: printed as written; English "Teirnon Twrf Liant" throughout, the note says the spelling differs.

## 2026-11-12 · mabinogi-004 · word division at col. 30
- "am gyflauan mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed" (unit 40): Evans prints *arýwnaethoed* as one run, so the division "ar y" is ours (from the witness). The sense wants *a ry wnaethoed* 'that she had done' (relative a + perfective ry; Red Book *ac a wnathoed*). Decided meanwhile: text left as established ("ar y"); the note explains it as *a ry*, and the glossary entries stand with either division. The owner may want the text re-divided "ac a ry wnaethoed" (a re-pin of the established text).

## 2026-11-12 · mabinogi-005 · small open points
- "tryded prif rieni yn yr ynys hon" (col. 40; units 31, 68): *rieni* read as 'ancestresses' (one of the Three Chief Ancestresses); it might be *rianed* 'maidens'. Decided meanwhile: 'Chief Ancestresses' in both places, the notes say the sense is uncertain.
- "ardiawc … yn ymdidan" (col. 44; unit 91): both manuscripts read *yn ymdidan*; the Red Book adds *amyuarth*, sense unclear. Decided meanwhile: text as the White Book, construed 'dull … in talk', flagged uncertain.
- Rare words left flagged uncertain in notes and glossary: *angassei*, *ymaruar*, *athrugar*, *anorles*, *eighaw*, *delediwaf*; *kyuref* kept with no modern form (perhaps *cyfref*; not confirmed).

## 2026-11-12 · mabinogi-006 · small open points (establish)
- Col. 49 l. 6: "carchara wynt ua na at trachefyn" — *ua* is certain on the image; the witness supplies "[ac]", the Red Book reads "hyt nat elont dracheuyn". Decided meanwhile: text as the White Book; the draft's note to read it as 'and do not let (them) back', flagged uncertain.
- Col. 52 l. 1: "ygwaelawt" (single g) divided "y gwaelawt" (as "y mywn"); the owner may prefer "yg waelawt" or the witness's one word.
- The englyn (col. 54) is set as a prose paragraph in quotes; the owner may want verse lines.

## 2026-11-12 · mabinogi-006 · small open points (draft)
- "pedeir degwlat a seithugeint" (col. 50; unit 27): read 'fourteen lands and seven score' = 154; the Red Book has *pedeir gwlat a seith ugeint* (144). Decided meanwhile: 154 in `l`/`i`, the note gives both and says the count is uncertain.
- "a wnathoedit" (col. 48; unit 12): possibly a slip for *a wnaethoedit*; not in the establish log and not rechecked on the image. Decided meanwhile: text as established, glossed as the pluperfect impersonal of gwneuthur.
- The englyn (unit 94): every rendering tentative (*kynniuyeit*, *rac kydwyr*); the owner may want it set as verse lines (see the establish point above).

## 2026-11-12 · mabinogi-007 · small open points (establish)
- Col. 58 l. 36: the White Book writes "Ac ar hynny o gin" at the foot of fol. 185v, then on the next leaf "A chyn amlyket … Ac ar hynny o ginyaw y buant seith mlyned" — the clause begun too early and written again in place. Decided meanwhile: printed as written, "Ac ar hynny o gin— A chyn amlyket …", the note to say so. The owner may prefer to drop the false start (a re-pin).
- Col. 57 l. 31: Evans prints "guae ni o'm ganedigaeth" (witness and Red Book *ui*). Decided meanwhile: *ni* kept; the note gives *ui*.
- Col. 60 l. 13: "kychu a'r penn" (witness *kyrchu*, Red Book *kychwynnu*). Decided meanwhile: kept as printed, flagged uncertain.
- Col. 57: "yglan Alaw" divided "y glan" as 006's "y gwaelawt"; same open point.
- source/drafts/mabinogi-007-ocr.txt carries a block of mabinogi-006's text inside col 56 (a setup-script fault); it did not affect the established text (col 56 read from the image). Not corrected (setup file).

## 2026-11-13 · mabinogi-007 · small open points (draft)
- "Guern gwngwch uiwch Uordwyt Tyllyon" (col. 56; unit 13): the cry is obscure. Decided meanwhile: left untranslated in `l` and `i`; the note says so, and the guesses were left out.
- "Da a dwy ynys" (unit 36; Red Book *ys da dwy ynys*): rendered 'two good islands', flagged uncertain.
- "Yspydawt Urdaul Benn" (unit 63): rendered 'the Hospitality of the Honoured Head' (urddol), built afresh from the Welsh.
- "pedeir decwlat a seithugeint" (unit 80): rendered as 154, consistent with 006's count; the note gives the Red Book's *deg wlat a seith ugeint*. Same open point as 006.
